neighbours.label: 1960s American politics: Lyndon Johnson's era and its civil-rights and Vietnam events, not other Johnsons or other presidential eras
fire: The Gulf of Tonkin Resolution passed Congress in August 1964 with barely any opposition.
Barry Goldwater lost badly in the 1964 presidential election, carrying only six states.
In his War on Poverty, President Johnson asked Congress to fund Head Start and food stamps.
The March on Washington in 1963 drew a quarter of a million people to the Lincoln Memorial.
Marchers were beaten on the Edmund Pettus Bridge, and the Voting Rights Act followed that summer.
Medicare was signed into law in 1965 at the Truman Library in Missouri.
Anti-war protesters chanted outside the White House as Lyndon Johnson sent more troops to Vietnam.
After the Watts riots of 1965, the Kerner Commission studied racial unrest in American cities.
quiet: The Louisiana Purchase passed the Senate in October 1803 with barely any opposition.
William Howard Taft lost badly in the 1912 presidential election, carrying only two states.
In his Fourteen Points, President Wilson asked Congress to back a league of nations.
The Bonus Army in 1932 brought thousands of veterans to camps along the Anacostia River.
Settlers were pushed west along the Oregon Trail, and the Homestead Act followed that decade.
Prohibition was written into law in 1919 by the Volstead Act in Congress.
Dwayne Johnson signed autographs outside the cinema as the fans lined up to see his latest action film.
After the Boston Tea Party of 1773, the British Parliament closed the harbour of the American port.

notes: Card: ' Johnson' x10, digits, ' King', 'ma'. Probes: Lyndon Johnson 0.87, Great Society 0.96, 1964 and 1968 about 0.39-0.41, Selma 0.51; Magic or Boris Johnson 0.05, Andrew Johnson 0.05, FDR 0.03, though Nixon and Carter reached 0.21. Tested on events without the word Johnson.
